what: Can the PAD reach the REAL block in our torch pairformer? Two controls, 48 blocks deep.
why: of3t-modelboundary measured the trunk gradient norm at 12.3912543630 with 8 pad rows and 43.2103398400 with 328, 3.487164x, on real inputs verified bit-identical between the two boundaries (checked pass 325: s_in and z_in real blocks agree to 0.0). D174 proposed a missing transition mask as the mechanism. This asks whether the model's SEMANTICS can produce any such dependence at all.
tree: wk/of3t-orchestrator, tt_bio/reference.py as shipped -- Transition.forward has no mask parameter
host: pc, CPU only, torch 2.8.0+cpu, no Tenstorrent device opened
non_vacuity: of3t-ditmodel found its own control vacuous twice: a freshly built Transition has a zero LayerNorm bias and a zeroed fc3, so it returns exactly 0 on a zero pad row whatever the mask does. Every zero-initialised parameter and every LayerNorm bias is forced non-zero here, and both controls assert the pad actually moved before reporting.

control_1_width.desc: same 56 real tokens padded to 64 and to 384

control_2_pad_value.desc: same width 384, pad filled 0.7 against -3.1 -- no reduction-extent confound

result: PAD VALUES: at 8 and at 48 blocks the pad output moves 7.7862e+02 between arms and the real block is BIT-IDENTICAL, absdiff exactly 0.0 on both the single and the pair track. PAD WIDTH: the real block differs 9.088062e-07 (s) and 6.316006e-07 (z) at 48 blocks, growing about linearly with depth from 6.09e-08 at one block -- the fp32 reduction-order floor, not a leak.
conclusion: Our pairformer's masking is semantically correct: the pad cannot reach the real block at any depth, and pad EXTENT moves it only at fp32 rounding. So the device's 3.487164x cannot be model semantics, and a transition output mask cannot fix a real-block answer that is already exact. D174's correctness framing is refuted; the extent sensitivity is a DEVICE effect and is reopened as its own object.
does_not_show: this is the torch reference with non-degenerate RANDOM weights, not the served checkpoint, and it is a FORWARD result. Masking could still suppress a device-side parameter-gradient contamination, because a parameter gradient reduces over pad positions and the device's pad cotangent is only known to be exactly zero AT THE BOUNDARY. That is what the MASKON arm and a mid-stack cotangent capture decide, and neither has run.
